messages:
sarah_support: Hey team, Acme reports intermittent DNS failures and TLS errors when hitting their private service endpoint service.acme.internal through Redwood Private. Started after they moved to a new resolver config in their VPC. They see NXDOMAIN from our platform sometimes, and when IPs resolve curl fails with 'certificate unknown'. They can reach it from public internet. Can we triage?

ian_oncall: thanks, Sarah. quick questions: 1) is this only for that tenant? 2) last successful timestamp? 3) do they use node-local caching or a managed resolver?

sarah_support: Only Acme for now. Last success ~1768887000 (approx). They mentioned switching to a third-party resolver appliance in their VPC and adding custom resolver rules. They also said they have an egress allowlist.

kelly_netops: likely culprits: split-horizon private hosted zone overlap OR resolver_rule that forwards to a resolver that returns NXDOMAIN for the private zone. Also the TLS 'certificate unknown' could be OCSP/CRL or missing intermediate certs.

mike_repro: I repro'd from a test VPC using their resolver config. dig +short service.acme.internal @10.0.2.2 -> sometimes returns IPs, often NXDOMAIN. When IP returns, curl -v https://10.1.4.22/ shows TLS alert: "unknown CA" from OpenSSL, not our Redwood cert. Means the server's cert chain is incomplete or client can't reach ocsp/ca.

kelly_netops: paste the dig +trace and dig @their-resolver outputs? also want to see the Route53 private hosted zones list for the tenant account. Might be duplicate hosted zone in another account shadowing records.

sarah_support: pasted from customer: ```dig @10.0.2.2 service.acme.internal +short
# sometimes:
10.1.4.22
# sometimes: nothing (NXDOMAIN)
```

mike_repro: captured TLS handshake: ```
* Connected to 10.1.4.22 (10.1.4.22) port 443
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 handshake, ClientHello
* handshake failed: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
``` Server cert chain from s_client: only leaf cert (Acme APISRV) returned, no intermediate. OCSP stapling not present.

ian_oncall: interesting. If the server sends incomplete chain, some clients accept (if they have intermediate locally) and others fail. But why NXDOMAIN intermittently? Suggests two different resolvers returned different answers — split-horizon or resolver failover to misconfigured forwarder.

kelly_netops: ask Acme whether their resolver appliance does health-check-based conditional forwarding. Could be it forwards to internal authoritative when healthy, otherwise forwards to a public resolver which doesn't have the private zone -> NXDOMAIN. Also check Route53 associations: if they detached a VPC from the private hosted zone during migration, our resolver might not be authorized for that zone anymore.

sarah_support: I've asked Acme to confirm VPC-owned Route53 associations and whether they added a forwarding rule to a new resolver. Pending.

mike_repro: also note the egress allowlist comment — if the client's VPC blocks outbound to CA/OCSP endpoints, browsers/clients might fail verification. But OpenSSL 'unknown ca' usually means missing chain or untrusted issuer, not OCSP. Still, check whether node-local forwarder or proxy is intercepting and doing TLS termination.

kelly_netops: good point. If there's a transparent proxy that substitutes certs, that could explain unknown CA. But customer said same IP from internet works. So proxy likely only inside VPC.

ian_oncall: action plan: 1) get Route53 private hosted zone id + VPC associations from Acme 2) ask for their resolver_rule list (conditional forwarders) 3) request tcpdump or packet capture from within their VPC showing DNS query/response (UDP/TCP) for the failing requests and a TLS s_client -showcerts output to verify chain 4) confirm egress allowlist entries (can they talk to CA OCSP/CRL endpoints and to Let's Encrypt/ACM endpoints if used).

sarah_support: I've sent that triage checklist. Acme returned: they have a private hosted zone Z12345 acme.internal, associated with two VPCs, but apparently during migration they temporarily disassociated the app VPC and then re-associated. They also have a resolver rule pointing service.acme.internal -> 10.0.2.2 (their appliance).

mike_repro: okay that fits. If appliance unhappy it may return NXDOMAIN, and when it returns an IP the appliance might be giving an internal VIP that terminates TLS with only leaf cert. Recommend we ask Acme to check their appliance's cert chain config and full server cert chain. Also check that their re-association completed and Route53 is healthy: ```aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z12345``` and ```aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters \"Name=tag:Name,Values=app-vpc\"```

kelly_netops: I'll also check on our side for any resolver_rule misrouting in Redwood Private. Not seeing global logs yet, can we get signed pcap or tcpdump from customer?

sarah_support: they uploaded a packet capture. I forwarded to you. Capture shows two DNS responses for same query within 200ms: one from 10.0.2.2 with ANSWER (A 10.1.4.22), then later a response from 169.254.169.253 (local forwarder) with RCODE=3 (NXDOMAIN). Looks like race between appliance and node-local cache/forwarder.

ian_oncall: that race is deadly. Node-local cache might be configured to fall back to another upstream when the appliance is slow/unhealthy. If the fallback upstream doesn't have the private zone, apps will get NXDOMAIN intermittently. Fix: ensure forwarder fallback respects the private zone or make the appliance authoritative/replicate zone.

kelly_netops: flagged a config bug in their node-local resolver fallback. Sent Acme a recommended change to stub-domains and conditional forwarding so the appliance is always preferred for the acme.internal zone, and increase timeout/retry to avoid fallback races.

mike_repro: separate TLS item: server returns incomplete chain. I asked them to re-import cert with full chain into their LB/terminator (leaf + intermediates). Also check that internal proxies aren't stripping intermediates.

sarah_support: Acme applied both fixes: 1) forced resolver_rule precedence to appliance; 2) reloaded cert chain on LB with intermediate. They reported 24 hours of testing with no NXDOMAIN and TLS handshakes now succeed.

ian_oncall: closing loop: recommend to customer to add monitoring for DNS volatility and to avoid fallback to public resolvers for private zones. Also suggested they use Route53 private hosted zone association verification post-migration.

kelly_netops: I'll create an internal KB entry summarizing this pattern: "resolver fallback + split-horizon private zone -> intermittent NXDOMAIN" + cert chain check for internal LB. Tag for eng-runtime: potential improvement: expose per-tenant resolver precedence metrics in Console.

deploy-bot: deployment event: created kb/triage-dns-resolver-fallback-2026-03-17 (sha: abc123) by kelly_netops

sarah_support: marking this thread resolved from support side. :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone!
